text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Britain's envoy on the Cyprus problem David Hannay recommends realism and give and take on both sides when they go to direct talks next month.
- Communist Akel tries to break the deadlock in its search for a presidential candidate for the opposition in next year's poll by putting forward the name of lawyer Marios Eliades.
- Hannay rebukes Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash for cancelling a meeting with him.
- New leadership in (right-wing) Democratic Rally party takes over.
- More than 100 Kurds and Grey Wolves clash in the (Turkish) occupied areas, injuring dozens.
- PEO trade union predicts an increase in the cost of living allowance for workers by around five percent at the end of July.

- The scene changes in the search for a common candidate in opposition camp. Marios Eliades has been added to the list which includes former president George Vassiliou, former foreign minister George Iakovou, parliamentary spokesman of centre-right Diko party Tassos Papadopoulos and former cabinet member Christos Mavrellis.
- A strategic plan for the development of the Cyprus Ports Authority drawn up by the Cyprus Development Bank is impossible to implement in practice.
- Hannay does not rule out the possibility that a new set of ideas will be proposed by the United Nations to help the negotiating process on Cyprus.
